**Cloudflare AI wallets test trust frameworks for agentic commerce**

*A major internet infrastructure provider entering agentic payments raises immediate questions about whether existing governance and liability frameworks can keep pace.*

Cloudflare has introduced AI wallets that allow autonomous software agents to initiate and settle payments on behalf of users, putting the nascent trust frameworks for agentic commerce under practical pressure. The product embeds payment capabilities into Cloudflare's infrastructure layer, positioning the company not as a payment processor but as a connectivity provider through which AI agents access commercial services.

The agentic payments conversation shifts here from bilateral arrangements between card networks and individual fintechs to the platform layer. Where previous agentic payment pilots from Visa, Mastercard and individual banks have operated within established scheme rules, Cloudflare's approach sits outside those structures and raises questions about who bears liability when an agent transacts on a user's behalf.

The parallels with the early standardisation phases of contactless payments and open banking are instructive. In both cases, commercial deployment ran ahead of formal trust frameworks, and regulators had to retrofit governance. The Financial Conduct Authority's ongoing AI governance work and the Payment Systems Regulator's authorised push payment liability rules both touch the question of agent-initiated transactions, but neither yet provides a comprehensive answer for the model Cloudflare is testing.

*Sources: [Cloudflare AI Wallets Put Agentic Commerce Trust Frameworks to the Test](https://thefintechtimes.com/cloudflare-ai-wallets-put-agentic-commerce-trust-frameworks-to-the-test/) — Thefintechtimes*

**Adyen hires Klarna's Niclas Neglen as its next chief financial officer**

*The appointment fills a vacancy created when Adyen's previous CFO left for AI startup ElevenLabs, and comes as Klarna revised its growth outlook downward.*

Adyen has nominated Niclas Neglen, currently chief financial officer at Klarna, as its next CFO and a member of its statutory management board, effective February 1, 2027. The appointment is subject to approval by the Dutch Central Bank and Adyen's shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting.

Neglen replaces Ethan Tandowsky, who left Adyen on August 31 to join AI company ElevenLabs. Hwa Tsao, Adyen's senior vice president of group finance, has been serving as interim CFO and will continue in that role until Neglen arrives. Neglen joined Klarna as CFO in 2021, having previously served as CFO and chief operating officer for Europe, the Middle East and Africa at HSBC Private Bank, and spent 13 years at General Electric in senior finance roles.

Klarna announced Neglen's planned departure on August 18, the same day it cut its full-year gross merchandise volume guidance to between $149 billion and $151 billion, down from a prior forecast of more than $155 billion. For Adyen, which co-founder and co-CEO Pieter van der Does says is seeking a CFO who understands its growth stage, the hire brings in a finance leader who has steered a major European fintech through its IPO period. Adyen confirmed it had made no changes to its financial objectives.

*Sources: [Adyen Names Klarna CFO Niclas Neglen as New Finance Chief](https://www.pymnts.com/personnel/2026/adyen-names-klarna-cfo-niclas-neglen-new-finance-chief/) — PYMNTS*

**Nubank in talks to acquire Monzo in deal worth up to £10bn**

*A takeover by Latin America's largest digital bank would be the biggest neobank acquisition to date, reshaping Monzo's recently launched European expansion and dealing a blow to London's IPO ambitions.*

Nu Holdings, the NYSE-listed parent of Brazilian digital bank Nubank, is in early-stage talks about acquiring Monzo in a deal that could value the UK challenger bank at between £8 billion and £10 billion. Sky News first reported the discussions on September 26, with Bloomberg and the Financial Times subsequently confirming that talks are under way.

A Nubank acquisition is one of two paths Monzo's board is weighing. The alternative is a new funding round, also expected to value the business at more than £8 billion, with proceeds earmarked for expansion into continental Europe. Monzo has separately been in discussions with private equity firms about selling up to a 15% stake. Both Monzo and Nubank declined to comment.

The timing is pointed. Monzo posted pre-tax profit of £87.3 million for the year to March, with revenue growing 39% to £1.7 billion, and it has 16 million customers. It secured a full European banking licence from the Central Bank of Ireland last December and launched Irish operations in April, but its EU chief executive, Michael Carney, announced his departure on September 22 and chair Gary Hoffman left in early September. Nubank, with a market capitalisation of roughly $65.5 billion, would gain an immediate presence in UK and European retail banking. For London, losing Monzo to an overseas acquirer rather than a domestic IPO would underscore the continuing difficulty of retaining fast-growing fintechs on British public markets.

*Sources: [Nubank Weighs $13 Billion Bid for Monzo](https://www.pymnts.com/news/banking/2026/nubank-weighs-13-billion-bid-for-monzo/) — PYMNTS*

**US prosecutors seize bank accounts of Tether-linked payment firm**

*The seizure intensifies scrutiny of the infrastructure connecting Tether to the traditional banking system, with potential implications for euro-denominated stablecoin strategies.*

US federal prosecutors have seized bank accounts belonging to Capstone, a payments business that has been processing transactions on behalf of stablecoin issuer Tether and its sister exchange Bitfinex, according to the Financial Times. The action signals that US law enforcement is targeting not just stablecoin issuers directly but the payment intermediaries that connect them to traditional banking rails.

The move comes as several European banking consortia are developing their own euro-denominated stablecoins, with one joint venture announced earlier this month making a euro token its priority. Tether's USDT remains the dominant stablecoin globally, but its relationship with the regulated banking system has always been its principal vulnerability. Enforcement actions against its payment partners narrow the corridors through which Tether can access dollar clearing, potentially accelerating the shift toward regulated, bank-issued alternatives.

European institutions developing stablecoin strategies under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation face a sharpening regulatory premium attached to transparent, fully licensed issuance. The contrast between Tether's intermediary-dependent model and the bank-backed structures emerging in Europe is becoming starker with each enforcement action.

*Sources: [US prosecutors seize Tether-linked payment firm's bank accounts - FT](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48478/us-prosecutors-seize-tether-linked-payment-firms-bank-accounts---ft?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
